subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit normal-chat tool-error delivery policy such as `all | final | off`, and what safety contract should `final` use before hiding a mutating or external-side-effect failure?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability gap, but choosing the default, final-only semantics, and side-effect safety boundary changes public config and user-visible failure behavior.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add an opt-in delivery enum that keeps current `all` behavior by default and defines conservative `final` and `off` semantics with schema, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep boolean suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator escape hatch and handle confusing warnings through docs or narrower issue-specific fixes.

options.title: Defer to recovery/status design
options.body: Leave this open until the warning reason, retry-confirmation, and internal-warning routing issues converge on a shared status model.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in delivery enum that keeps current `all` behavior by default and defines conservative `final` and `off` semantics with schema, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-history signal on the warning-policy path and merged related acknowledged-failure behavior.
